google.help: What Google itself reports, kept apart from the settings above. Until Search Console is connected, the figures below are a sample of what will show.
google.connectHelp: This needs the website’s owner and setup outside the Website Manager:
google.step1: Verify the domain (orgtik.ch, or the live domain) in Google Search Console, with a DNS TXT record.
google.step2: Create a Google Cloud project, enable the Search Console API, and set up OAuth consent or a service account.

where.family: /services → department cards, /services/'{family}' → family heading and service list, and About → capability cards. These fields describe the family; individual services are edited separately.
where.service: /services → searchable service cards; /services/'{family}' → service cards; /services/'{family}'/'{service}' → service heading, introduction and capability labels. Pricing and package contents use a separate purchasing catalog.
where.software: Home → software diagram; /software → system cards; /software/'{system}' → detail heading, introduction and feature cards. Home uses Short label; the software page uses Formal name. Purchasing labels and prices come from a separate catalog.
where.highlights: /software/'{system}' → feature section below the detail introduction. The first item is the large lead card; later items form the supporting cards. Task labels use the matching position in the system Tasks list.
where.useCases: /software/'{system}' → use-case section after the feature cards. Titles appear in the selector; the selected item supplies the visible title and description. Use-case images are chosen by the website template.
where.article: /insights → article cards; /insights/'{article}' → title, excerpt and takeaway panel near the beginning of the article. Article SEO is separate from these visible words.
where.articleBody: /insights/'{article}' → reading column after the cover and takeaway panel. Section order controls reading order. Each section shows its heading, then its text, image and video blocks in order.
where.legal: /legal/'{document}' → selected document title and introduction; the title also labels its entry in the legal document navigation. The page-level introduction is edited in Pages → Legal.
where.legalBody: /legal/'{document}' → document reading area below its title and summary. Every saved section supplies a heading and body paragraph; changing order changes document reading order.
where.roadmap: /roadmap → milestone timeline, filtered by period, year, theme and search. Selecting a milestone opens its detail dialog. These records are separate from community suggestions in Marketing → Ideas.
where.caseBrief: /work → project cards; /work/'{project}' → project heading and Brief section. Client facts, challenge, goal, role and highlight require a full published story with approved or explicitly labelled sample results. Card-only projects do not show those story fields.
where.approach: /work/'{project}' → section 02, after the Brief. Requires a full published story. The department determines its layout: design journal, development log, marketing schedule, support tickets or hosting runbook.
where.delivered: /work/'{project}' → section 03 after Approach. Requires a full published story. The department selects a design board, system architecture, campaign week, support priorities or hosting component-status view.
where.results: /work/'{project}' → section 04 after Delivered work. Requires a full published story. The department selects metrics, gauges, marketing charts, support comparisons or a hosting performance chart. Sample figures retain their sample label until approved.

hints.chartCutover: Hosting Results → migration marker on the performance chart. This is a point count separating before/after data, not a visible date label.
hints.monthlyBaseline: Marketing Results → monthly bars. Counts how many leading points use the baseline style; later points use the campaign style.
hints.series: Chart points are ordered label/value pairs. The label appears on the time axis; the number determines chart height and its accessible description.
hints.funnel: Marketing Results → conversion funnel. Each pair is stage label then numeric count; the website calculates the rate against the preceding stage.
hints.channels: Marketing Results → channel mix. Each pair stores the channel name then its percentage share; the value controls segment width and the visible percentage.
hints.touchpointImage: Design Delivered work → application image. The current renderer prefixes /assets/ to this stored filename; use the existing asset-path format.
hints.familyIcon: Icon on department cards and family service rows; it does not replace the family cover image.
hints.softwareIcon: Home software diagram nodes and the software-detail use-case panel. Changing this icon does not change icons in the separate purchasing catalog.
hints.articleCategory: Associates the article with a service family. The website displays that family’s Short label on article cards, category filters and the article heading.
hints.articleDate: Displayed on article cards and in article facts; also used in structured article metadata. This is separate from the publishing schedule.
hints.readingMinutes: Minutes shown on article cards, the article heading and article facts. The website formats the unit; enter the number only.
hints.familyImage: /services → family cards and expanded family-service illustrations; service-detail capability cards reuse the family image. It does not replace each project’s images.
hints.softwareImage: /software/'{system}' → illustration in the feature section. Related-system cards may also use it. Home’s software diagram uses icons, and use-case images additionally use template assets.
hints.articleImage: /insights → article cards and /insights/'{article}' → cover above the takeaway panel. Images inserted between paragraphs are edited separately in the article body.
hints.projectImage: /work → project card image, also available as the project’s fallback social image. The project gallery is a separate collection and is not replaced by this cover.
hints.imageAlt: Used by the entry’s social/search image metadata. The current page templates use their own visible captions or placeholder labels, so this text is not a visible section heading.
